newsitem.title: UK: MATIF hopes to top CSCE with new sugar contract.
newsitem.headline: MATIF hopes to top CSCE with new sugar contract.

text.p: France's MATIF futures exchange hopes to succeed with its new lesser-quality white sugar contract where New York's CSCE exchange failed, MATIF officials said on Thursday.
MATIF plans to launch a 100 ICUMSA sugar contract on June 20 to benefit both trade players and key producers of lesser-quality white sugars such as Brazil, they said.
MATIF had embarked on a feasibility study to investigate a new contract to reflect changes in world markets, including the surge in lower whites qualities.
"We saw during the feasibility study...why the most successful market in the world of sugar failed to succeed with 100 ICUMSA," said Bruno Guiot, Commodities Product Manager at the Paris-based MATIF.

Speaking at a news conference in London, Guiot said the huge activity in raw sugar futures prevented hard-pressed New York brokers from putting human resources towards the development of any new contract.
White sugar also presented more technical problems than raw sugar, he added.
"New York tried many times to develop a white sugar market. But the white market is quite technical, much more than the raw market," Guiot said.
Trading began in New York's white sugar futures contract, also with a maximum of 100 ICUMSA, on the CSCE last June. But volume and open interest has been patchy.
Sugars with ratings close to 100 ICUMSA are mainly produced in South America, Central America and Asia and currently account for over a third of world sugar trade.
Other sugars with ICUMSA ratings of under 45 are mainly produced in Europe.
ICUMSA (International Commission for Uniform Method of Sugar Analysis) ratings measure the colouring of sugar and are an indication of quality.

MATIF, founded in February 1986, is one of the world's largest financial futures and options exchanges with more than 68 million contracts traded in 1996, including more than 272,000 commodities contracts.
